subject: art-design
title: Site-Specific Art: Goldsworthy and Eliasson
welcome_lead: Place is medium. The work cannot move without losing its meaning.
meta_desc: A-Level Art & Design: site-specific art, Andy Goldsworthy and Olafur Eliasson.

concepts.def: Art designed for and inseparable from its location.
British sculptor (b. 1956), ephemeral works in landscape.
1960s-70s movement using landscape as site and material.
Existing briefly — the work decays or is documented.
Eliasson's 2003 installation at Tate Modern's Turbine Hall.

walkthroughs.body_html: Andy Goldsworthy arranges leaves, ice, stone and wood in situ, photographing the result. The photograph becomes the durable artwork — the sculpture itself returns to nature.

Olafur Eliasson's The Weather Project (Tate Modern, 2003) flooded the Turbine Hall with mono-frequency yellow light and a half-sun mirrored to a full disc on the ceiling. Two million visitors lay beneath it.
Site-specific work resists the museum's neutralising 'white cube'. Robert Smithson, Walter De Maria and the Land Artists argued that place — geology, climate, history — is part of the artwork.
